subject: Encryption artifacts for security review — SilverLake onboarding

From: Claire Wu <claire.wu@silverlakepartners.com>

Cc: SL-ExternalAudit <security-requests@silverlakepartners.com>
Date: 2027-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Encryption artifacts requested for SilverLake onboarding

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding call this morning. As part of SilverLake's security checklist we need a compact set of cryptographic artifacts to complete our SIG/SOC2 intake for the initial tenancy. To keep the review tight, could you provide the following by end-of-day tomorrow (PST)?

- Keystore inventory (logical names, created_at, key types, KMS/HSM owner)
- Recent rotation log excerpt (last 90 days) showing rotation events and operator IDs
- HSM attestation summary (model, firmware, serial, attestation date)
- Short note on envelope-wrapping / KEK/DEK flow for tenant BYOK (1–2 paragraphs)

We can accept CSV/TXT/PDF stubs. If there are any access constraints for downloadable artifacts, please include a Drive link or DocuSign where relevant.

Claire Wu
Security Operations | SilverLake Partners
claire.wu@silverlakepartners.com
+1 415-555-0198

[This request is tied to SilverLake onboarding ID: SL-ONB-8023]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Claire Wu <claire.wu@silverlakepartners.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Encryption artifacts requested for SilverLake onboarding

Claire,

Thanks — we can get that to you. Attaching a compact bundle and a short operational note below. Quick notes:

1) Attachments included in this email (stubs):
   - keystore_inventory.csv (CSV, 12KB) — logical id, key type, created_at, owner, HSM-backed boolean
   - rotation_log_excerpt.txt (TXT, 9KB) — rotation events, operator id, rationale tag, rotation method
   - hsm_attestation_summary.pdf (PDF, 45KB) — manufactured attestation statements and firmware snapshot

2) BYOK envelope flow (summary):
   Redwood uses a KEK (Key Encryption Key) stored in the customer-dedicated HSM for wrapping tenant DEKs (Data Encryption Keys). DEKs are generated per-tenant within our runtime and wrapped with the tenant KEK before persistent storage. Rotation occurs via an orchestrated key-roll procedure that creates a new DEK and re-wraps references; KEK rotations require an HSM key ceremony and are recorded in our rotation ledger. Access to KEK material is limited to HSM roles; plaintext KEKs are never exported.

Irene and Jonas — looping you in for any gaps. Ben, if the compliance team prefers a signed attestation from our HSM vendor, can you advise?

Thanks,

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Trust & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Encryption artifacts requested for SilverLake onboarding

Claire — quick follow-up with implementation-level context and a small clarifying ask.

Implementation notes:
- Keystore inventory: the CSV includes a boolean field 'hsm_backed' and a 'wrapping_algorithm' column. Tenant BYOK keys are labeled with the tenant id prefix.
- Rotation ledger: our rotation_log_excerpt shows the event id, key_id, timestamp, operator (RBAC id), and whether rewrap was full or incremental.
- HSM attestation: the PDF is an exported vendor attestation snapshot (no private key material).

Clarifying ask: do you need operator-level audit traces (syslog/journal entries) for the rotation events, or is the rotation ledger + operator RBAC id sufficient for your intake? If you need syslog extracts we can produce a redacted sample (remove IPs and session tokens).

Jonas, can you confirm the rotation ledger export format is acceptable for SilverLake and if we should redact any fields before sharing?

Irene Choi
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Received the bundle, thanks for the quick turnaround. The CSV and PDF look good. For completeness during the SOC2 intake we do ask for a short redacted syslog excerpt for one rotation event so we can map the ledger entry to an observable system trace in our timeline. If you can provide a single redacted syslog extract (remove IPs, session tokens, and any tenant data) that shows the rotation workflow (timestamp, process id, user/rbac id, rotation command), that will close out SL-ONB-8023 on our side.

If it's easier, a 3–5 line sample in TXT is fine. Otherwise we can accept a Drive link with viewer-only access.
